title: Hey ASR System! Why Aren’t You More Inclusive? Automatic Speech Recognition Systems’ Bias and Proposed Bias Mitigation Techniques. A Literature Review.

bias_targets.methodology: Synthesizing studies that measure Word Error Rate (WER) disparities between demographic groups (e.g., Black vs. White speakers), assess speech recognition performance on dialects like African American Vernacular English (AAVE), and evaluate accuracy differences for various regional accents and non-native speakers.

Reviewing literature that compares ASR performance (WER) between male and female speakers, quantifies gender imbalances in training corpora, and analyzes conversational agents' qualitative responses to gendered and sexualized prompts.

Surveying research that calculates ASR performance gaps (using WER and Character Error Rate) between speakers with health conditions or speech impairments (e.g., dysarthria, Parkinson's disease, Deaf/Hard of Hearing) and healthy controls, alongside qualitative user accessibility surveys for blind individuals.
